newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends down on exports and options.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends down on exports and options.

text.p: CBOT wheat closed lower on light exports with the market seeking direction after the late fund and local-related plunge in prices Tuesday, traders said.

Traders said there was nothing to drive the market one way or another leaving the market vulnerable to further declines. But aggressive put buying in options by a commercial may have lent pressure on prices in late trading, they said.

Technical traders said there now were bearish signs from the four and 20 day moving averages and the nine day relative strength index for December at 42.13 points as of Tuesday's close provided little direction.
There were no bullish surprises in recent USDA data.
USDA Tuesday said 73 percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop had been seeded as of Sunday, about as expected.
The market was expecting a 70 to 72 percent seeding completion pace and the average pace for U.S. winter wheat sowings is 74 percent.
But the four key soft red winter wheat states of Ohio, Indiana, Illinois and Missouri showed the seedings at 31 percent, below the average pace of 50 percent.
Wheat closed three to eight cents per bushel lower, with December down 4-1/2 cents at $4.17-1/4.
Rosenthal Collins sold three million bushels of December, O'Connor and Co sold one million December and R.J. O'Brien sold 1.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, down from 16,849 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, bought 1,000 December $4.00 puts at 1-3/4 to 2-1/4 cents and LIT America bought 800 December $4.80 calls at 1/2 to 3/8 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, up from 3,999 Tuesday.
